explanations: It was first made in Han China as a device for divination, and only adopted for navigation under the Song, in the 11th century.
The angle between true north and magnetic north is called magnetic declination, and it varies from place to place.
Its angles run clockwise from north at 0°, so east is 90°, south is 180° and west is 270°.
The magnetised needle turns on a low-friction pivot, in better ones a jewel bearing, and settles after a few seconds.
It is a device that shows the cardinal directions for navigation, usually with a needle, card or rose that aligns with magnetic north.

sources.excerpt: Among the Four Great Inventions, the magnetic compass was first invented as a device for divination as early as the Chinese Han dynasty (since c. 206 BC), and later adopted for navigation by the Song dynasty Chinese during the 11th century.
Depending on where the compass is located on the surface of the Earth the angle between true north and magnetic north, called magnetic declination can vary widely with geographic location.
Compasses often show angles in degrees: north corresponds to 0°, and the angles increase clockwise, so east is 90°, south is 180°, and west is 270°.
The needle is mounted on a low-friction pivot point, in better compasses a jewel bearing, so it can turn easily.
When the compass is held level, the needle turns until, after a few seconds to allow oscillations to die out, it settles into its equilibrium orientation.

A compass is a device that shows the cardinal directions used for navigation and geographic orientation. It typically consists of a magnetized needle or another element, such as a compass card or compass rose, that pivots to align itself with magnetic north.
